session_covered: US session of Tuesday 3 November (US midterm election day)
intro: Covers the US session of Tuesday 3 November (US midterm election day). Sent on the 08:15 retry; SPI 200 futures sources disagreed on level, so that figure is approximate (see notes).
footnotes: US index closes per Yahoo Finance. VIX per Yahoo Finance (prior close 21.15; FNArena showed 21.32 for Monday). 10-year yield per Yahoo Finance (^TNX 4.952%); Trading Economics showed 4.96%. AUD/USD, gold and iron ore are Trading Economics CFD-based reference prices; other sources showed gold between US$3,921 and US$3,932/oz. Brent is the CNBC settlement (down US$1.17); intraday quotes ranged from about US$102 to US$106.

setup.summary: SPI 200 futures are down about 0.3% (TradingView -0.26% at around 8,864; Stockhead -0.3%). Applied to the ASX 200's prior close of 8,886.8 (+30.3 points, +0.34%, after the RBA's 25bp hike to 4.85%), that implies an open about 23 points (0.26%) lower, near 8,864. Investing.com showed the December contract down 0.80% at 8,853.5, but that quote is a day-session close and is treated as stale. The soft lean contrasts with a firmer US session and reflects uncertainty around the US midterm results and the RBA hike.

local_events: No major scheduled Australian data release or RBA speech was confirmed in the sources checked; market reaction to Tuesday's RBA decision (6-3 vote) and post-decision commentary continues.
what_moved: The S&P 500 broke a three-day losing run, and the Nasdaq Composite rose 0.83%, as chip stocks rebounded on US election day, while the Dow slipped 0.38%. Brent fell for a second day on hopes of US-Iran diplomacy, though reports of a US strike on Iran's Qeshm Island kept oil volatile. Apple fell after warning that memory-chip costs would pressure margins. Sector breakdown for the S&P 500 was not available.

news.headline: RBA lifts cash rate to 4.85%.
news.summary: The Reserve Bank raised the cash rate by 25bp, its fifth hike this year and an 18-year high, in a 6-3 vote; three members wanted no change.

news.headline: ASX 200 closes higher after the hike.
news.summary: The index recovered from an initial dip to finish up 0.34% at 8,886.8.

news.headline: US midterms in focus.
news.summary: Polls closed with prediction markets favouring a Democratic House; JPMorgan expects a Democratic sweep could lower the S&P 500 by about 0.5%.

news.headline: Oil down again on Iran diplomacy hopes.
news.summary: Brent settled at US$103.60/bbl after Monday's 7.6% plunge, even as reports of a US strike on Qeshm Island emerged.

news.headline: Goldman lifts Brent forecast.
news.summary: Goldman Sachs raised its December Brent forecast to US$105 from US$90.

news.headline: US 10-year yield edges up.
news.summary: The yield rose to about 4.95% ahead of the election results.

news.headline: Australian dollar slips below US$0.70.
news.summary: The currency hit a two-week low after the split RBA decision.

coming_up: US midterm election results arrive today (Wednesday 4 November, Sydney time), with the market reaction to follow.
